searchSummary: Expanded primary-source survey through 2026-09-27, now including historical and current palettes Δ+1, degree+1 lists, (1+ε)Δ, Brooks Δ and Δ−1, degeneracy κ, chromatic-gap decisions; dynamic adaptivity, stream robustness, communication versus graph queries, and memory regimes remain separate. Every entry has a primary-paper link and explicit assumptions. Symbolic bounds remain unshaded where no common numeric axes justify interpolation. LCA coverage now separates deterministic degree+1 lists, randomized MIS-reduction, and average-case exact k-coloring. The bibliography is an evolving atlas, not a systematic review of every graph class and theorem.

coverage.note: Nine maintenance records from eight primary papers, plus a separately scoped decision lower bound. GH2026 v2 and AY2026 v1 are preprint claims to appear at SODA 2027; their theorem statements and models were checked. Amortized and worst-case guarantees remain separate.
Insertion/turnstile, randomized/deterministic, robust adaptive-output, Brooks palettes, degeneracy and chromatic-gap decisions are distinct slices.
Tight deterministic bipartite scale, randomized bounds, and separately labeled broader settings.
Centralized Δ+1 list-color LCAs, deterministic oblivious historical LCA, and average-case exact k-color LCA are distinct slices; worst-case exact-k LCA is not inferred from average-case result.
Randomized and deterministic LOCAL rounds separated; FOCS 2024 color results follow reductions. No unsupported lower frontier drawn.
Near-linear machine memory and strongly sublinear machine memory separated; deterministic low-memory result allows exponential local computation.
Adjacency-list/array slices are separated below; inspect each oracle and output assumption.
Adjacency-matrix slices are separated below; inspect pair-query and output assumptions.
Combined, communication, same-cluster, or other query interfaces are kept separate from pure list/matrix access.
A planted model with adversarial additions and explicitly conditional low-density hardness.
